key_impacts: Strong earthquake offshore Eastern Samar triggered a Tsunami Alert Level 3 (immediate evacuation) for multiple Philippine provinces.
Many coastal residents evacuated; surveyed barangays reported an estimated average of about 80% evacuating after the alert.
No significant tsunami wave appeared and no damages were observed; the alert was later cancelled.
Communication issues (power cuts, mobile outages, one incorrect radio broadcast) delayed/distorted messages to coastal communities.
In parts of Guiuan, expected wave travel time (~10 minutes) was shorter than the alert release (~14 minutes post-quake).
evidence_snippets: On 31 August 2012 a strong earthquake occurred in the Philippine Trench east of the southern tip of Eastern Samar.
PHIVOLCS issued alert level 3… immediate evacuation… for Northern Samar, Eastern Samar, Leyte, Southern Leyte, Surigao del Norte and Surigao del Sur.
However, no significant wave appeared and no damages were observed; PHIVOLCS later issued a tsunami alert cancellation statement.
missing_information: Observed tsunami heights, if any, along the coast
Detailed damage or casualty figures (none reported)

key_impacts: A tsunami alert was raised in the Philippines following the distant-source Chile earthquake and tsunami.
Because the source was distant, time was not a major factor in the related survey.
evidence_snippets: A similar survey… after a tsunami alert was raised in the end of February 2010; the source of the wave was distant (Chile).
Like the Chile earthquake of 27 February 2010…
